'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[Russian invasion of Ukraine]]
**[[List of military aid to Ukraine during the Russo-Ukrainian War|Military aid to Ukraine during the Russo-Ukrainian War]]
***The [[United States]] announces an $800 million aid package for [[Ukraine]] that includes [[cluster munition]]s for the first time. While the weapons are outlawed by over 100 countries under the [[Convention on Cluster Munitions]], the United States, Ukraine, and Russia are not signatories. [https://edition.cnn.com/2023/07/07/politics/cluster-munitions/index.html (CNN)]
***The U.S. package also includes [[M777 howitzer|M777 howitzers]], munitions for [[MIM-104 Patriot]] and [[M142 HIMARS]] missile systems, [[anti-tank weapons]], [[Unmanned aerial vehicle|UAVs]], and additional [[Bradley Fighting Vehicle]]s and [[Stryker]] [[armoured personnel carrier]]s. [https://www.reuters.com/world/us-cluster-munitions-ukraine-expected-fridays-800m-aid-package-2023-07-07/ (Reuters)]
*Spillover of the [[Somali Civil War (2009–present)|Somali Civil War]]
**Six [[Kenya Army|Kenyan soldiers]] and 23 [[Al-Shabaab (militant group)|Al-Shabaab]] members are killed during a [[shootout]] in Orgene village, [[Mandera County]], [[Kenya]]. Eight other soldiers are injured. [https://www.voanews.com/a/kenya-special-forces-kill-23-al-shabab-militants-/7171526.html (VOA)]
*[[Jihadist insurgency in Burkina Faso]]
**[[Jihadism|Jihadists]] kill at least 22 [[civilian]]s in two separate attacks in [[Namentenga Province]], [[Burkina Faso]]. [https://english.alarabiya.net/News/world/2023/07/08/Suspected-extremists-kill-22-in-Burkina-Faso-Sources (AFP via Al Arabiya)]
*[[Rohingya genocide]]
**Six [[Rohingya refugees in Bangladesh|Rohingya refugees]] are killed at the [[Kutupalong refugee camp|Kutupalong camp]] in [[Ukhia Upazila|Ukhia]], [[Cox's Bazar District|Cox's Bazar]], [[Bangladesh]], amidst clashes between rival [[Insurgency|insurgent groups]], the [[Arakan Rohingya Salvation Army]] and [[Rohingya Solidarity Organisation]]. [https://www.manilatimes.net/2023/07/09/world/six-killed-in-rohingya-camps-after-icc-prosecutors-visit/1899798 (AFP via ''The Manila Times'')]
*[[Israeli–Palestinian conflict]]
**[[Israel Defense Forces|Israeli soldiers]] shoot dead two [[Popular Front for the Liberation of Palestine]] [[militant]]s during a raid at a house in [[Nablus]] in the occupied [[West Bank]]. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/world-middle-east-66132367 (BBC News)]

'''Business and economy'''
*[[Land reform in the Philippines]]
**[[President of the Philippines|President]] [[Bongbong Marcos]] signs into law the [[New Agrarian Emancipation Act]], [[Debt relief|canceling]] over {{Philippine peso|57.56 billion|link=yes}} ([[United States dollar|US$]]1.04bn) in [[Agriculture in the Philippines|agricultural]] debt for more than 500,000 farmers. [https://www.channelnewsasia.com/asia/philippines-writes-us1-billion-farmer-debt-boost-food-production-3612951 (AFP via CNA)]
*[[2021–present United Kingdom cost-of-living crisis]]
**[[United Kingdom|British]] [[movie theater|cinema]] chain [[Empire Cinemas]] collapses into [[administration (law)|administration]] with the immediate loss of 150 jobs. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/business-66134084 (BBC News)]
*The [[China Securities Regulatory Commission]] imposes fines of nearly US$1 billion and $415 million on [[Science and technology in China|technology]] companies [[Ant Group]] and [[Tencent]], respectively, for violating [[financial regulation]]s and anti-[[money laundering]] obligations. [https://www.france24.com/en/live-news/20230707-china-fines-ant-group-almost-us-1-bn-as-tech-crackdown-draws-to-close (AFP via France 24)]

'''Disasters and accidents'''
*[[2023 Pakistan floods]]
**At least 55 people, including eight children, are killed by floods caused by [[monsoon]] rains in [[Pakistan]]. [https://apnews.com/article/pakistan-rains-deaths-flood-warning-3261921e01974c0aaf1cc28baafcb5bb (AP)]
*Six people are killed and 81 others are injured in a fire at a [[nursing home]] in [[Milan]], [[Lombardy]], [[Italy]]. [https://apnews.com/article/milan-nursing-home-fire-italy-bc84b572796d7fdf66deb27415b21be6 (AP)]
*At least 128 people are hospitalized in [[Sistan and Baluchestan province]], [[Iran]], due to [[dust storm]]s. [https://kalingatv.com/world/sandstorms-in-iran-send-over-800-people-to-hospitals/ (Xinhua)]
*Fourteen people are killed, six are missing, and three are injured after an apartment building collapsed in [[Recife]], [[Pernambuco]], [[Brazil]]. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-latin-america-66140720 (BBC News)]
*Six people are killed in an [[explosion]] at a [[chemical factory]] in [[Chapayevsk]], [[Samara Oblast]], [[Russia]]. [https://tass.com/emergencies/1643769 (TASS)]
*Two people are killed and another is missing due to a fire at an [[oil platform]] owned by Mexican state-owned company [[Pemex]] in the southern edge of [[Gulf of Mexico]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/americas/fire-breaks-out-pemex-offshore-platform-cantarell-complex-source-2023-07-07/ (Reuters)]
*Seventy-five [[Tourism in Ecuador|tourists]] become stranded overnight in [[Quito]], [[Ecuador]], when a [[glitch]] halts the [[TelefériQo]] [[gondola lift]], requiring a ten-hour rescue operation. [https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/news/international/us/dozens-rescued-after-being-stranded-overnight-in-worlds-highest-cable-car-systems-due-to-technical-glitch/articleshow/101581002.cms (''The Economic Times'')]

'''International relations'''
*[[China–Japan relations]]
**[[China]]'s [[General Administration of Customs]] announces a ban on food [[import]]s from ten [[Japanese prefecture]]s, citing [[Radiation effects from the Fukushima Daiichi nuclear disaster|safety concerns]] over [[Japan]]'s plan to [[Discharge of radioactive water of the Fukushima Daiichi Nuclear Power Plant|discharge]] [[Wastewater treatment|treated]] [[radioactive waste]] water from the [[Fukushima Daiichi Nuclear Power Plant]] into the [[Pacific Ocean]]. [https://www.lemonde.fr/en/international/article/2023/07/07/china-bans-some-japanese-food-imports-over-fukushima-water-release_6045114_4.html (AFP via ''Le Monde'')]
*[[U.S. President]] [[Joe Biden]] declares the complete [[Destruction of chemical weapons|destruction]] of [[United States chemical weapons program|the country's chemical weapons stockpile]], making the U.S. the last signatory of the [[Chemical Weapons Convention]] to destroy declared stockpiles and marking the elimination of all known global reserves of [[chemical weapon]]s. [https://www.rte.ie/news/2023/0708/1393468-chemical-weapons/ (AFP via RTÉ)]

'''Law and crime'''
*[[2023 Odisha train collision]]
**[[India]]'s [[Central Bureau of Investigation]] arrests two [[Indian Railway Service of Signal Engineers|signal engineers]] and a [[Track maintenance|technician]] on charges of [[culpable homicide]] and [[evidence tampering]] over last month's deadly [[train collision]] in [[Balasore district|Balasore]], [[Odisha]]. [https://apnews.com/article/india-train-accident-8725f8544f052768775a15c7682ad161 (AP)]
*[[2019 El Paso shooting]]
**Perpetrator [[Patrick Crusius]] is [[Criminal sentencing in the United States|sentenced]] to 90 consecutive [[Life imprisonment in the United States|life terms]] in a [[federal prison]] after pleading guilty to [[Hate crime laws in the United States|hate crimes]] related to the [[mass shooting]] in [[El Paso]], [[Texas]], United States. [https://www.manilatimes.net/2023/07/08/world/90-life-sentences-for-gunman-who-targeted-hispanics-in-texas/1899700 (AFP via ''The Manila Times'')]
*[[2019 Whakaari / White Island eruption]]
**Three [[tour operator]]s plead guilty to failing to ensure the health and safety of workers and tourists under the [[Health and Safety at Work Act 2015]] during the deadly [[Explosive eruption|eruption]] of [[Whakaari / White Island|White Island]] in [[New Zealand]] in 2019. They each face a maximum fine of [[New Zealand dollar|$]]1.5 million (US$927,000). [https://apnews.com/article/new-zealand-white-island-volcano-trial-c683fac2073ef10c240c97a9b0b3c25a (AP)]

'''Politics and elections'''
*In the [[Netherlands]], the [[fourth Rutte cabinet]] [[Demissionary cabinet|collapses]] amid disagreements over [[asylum application]]s. [[Prime Minister of the Netherlands|Prime Minister]] [[Mark Rutte]] announces that he will submit his [[resignation]] on Saturday. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-europe-66139789 (BBC News)]
